messages:
matt-sre: heads up — seeing disproportionate traffic to endpoints on node-gpu-05 for inference-svc in us-east-1, others almost idle. spike in 502s + client retries.
opsbot: [ALERT] inference-svc latency spike: p50=310ms p95=1.2s; error rate +4.8% (trigger rule: svc-latency).
sara-eng: can you paste ipvs table / kube-proxy mode? suspect ipvs scheduling issue or conntrack evictions.
matt-sre: sure, from node-gpu-05 (shortened):
```
# ipvsadm -Ln --numeric
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> 10.244.8.7:8080              sh
    -> 10.244.8.7:8080           Masq    1      0          0
    -> 10.244.9.3:8080           Masq   73      0      12345
    -> 10.244.10.4:8080          Masq    2      0       2345
```
Looks like one endpoint getting ~73 refcnt while others tiny.
hailey-mlinfra: fyi we rolled RoCE/nic MTU=9000 on all GPU nodes last week for RDMA; non-GPU nodes still at 1500. Could cause fragmentation or path MTU issues for east-west.
mike-net: confirmed via tcpdump on ToR — ICMP frag-needed for pod IPs routed between mgmt-nodes and gpu-nodes. Also saw repeated TCP retransmits then RSTs when packets hit the path MTU limit.
matt-sre: that would explain why kube-proxy keeps routing to same pod (connections drop to others?) — if some nodes fail TCP handshake intermittently, IPVS may mark them as 'down' or weight-effectively lowered.
sara-eng: also check conntrack entries. If SNAT is used, hashing may pick a pod that then fails and clients retry picking same backend.
mike-net: quick checks I ran:
```
# on non-gpu node
ip link show eth0 mtu 1500
# on gpu node
ip link show eth0 mtu 9000
# tcpdump
14:02:12.345678 IP 10.244.9.3.8080 > 10.244.8.7.43210: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
14:02:12.346123 IP 10.244.8.7 > 10.244.9.3: ICMP frag needed, mtu 1500
```
mike-net: suggested mitigations: ensure uniform MTU across pod network (set to 1500 or enable jumbo everywhere), or enable PMTU probing `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` as short term. Also check if RDMA offloads bypass iptables/ipvs — RoCE can interact badly with skb checksums, try toggling GRO/TSO/GSO.
hailey-mlinfra: we can flip GPU nodes back to 1500 quickly (rollback RoCE mtu) for canary, and schedule RDMA reprovisioning with proper network/ToR changes.
matt-sre: another note — kube-proxy is ipvs with scheduler 'sh' (source-hash) so SNAT differences and asymmetric path can cause sticky behavior. We could try `--ipvs-scheduler rr` temporarily to see distribution change.
sara-eng: also found conntrack evictions during the spike: `conntrack -L | grep inference-svc` showed many TIME_WAIT/UNREPLIED entries. Might be TCP resets from fragmentation.
leon-product: customers are seeing higher latencies and retries on model calls, any ETA on mitigation?
matt-sre: short plan: 1) set tcp_mtu_probing=1 cluster-wide (immediate) 2) roll gpu nodes to 1500 MTU as quick rollback 3) toggle kube-proxy scheduler to rr in a canary 4) monitor errors. rolling changes in next 10m.
opsbot: [ACTION] Created incident-1234 and assigned to eng-sre.
matt-sre: applied tcp_mtu_probing=1 on pilot nodes and disabled GRO on node-gpu-05: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off`. observing now.
hailey-mlinfra: we started a MTU rollback on two GPU nodes.
matt-sre: 20m after mitigation: retries down from ~5% to 0.7%, traffic distribution across endpoints is balanced now. keeping monitor for 2 hours. :thumbsup:
leon-product: thanks, keep me posted if we need to spin capacity.
sara-eng: follow-ups: open a ticket to standardize pod MTU for RDMA plans and document kube-proxy scheduler implications with SNAT for consistent-hash.
mike-net: I'll draft network changes for enabling jumbo frames end-to-end if we want permanent RoCE.
matt-sre: closing thread when monitor window ends, but saving ipvs+tcpdump snippets to incident-1234.
opsbot: Incident-1234 status: monitoring — no active alerts.
